I will keep this year simple and stable: I will run the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits the climate, the irrigation pattern, the machinery I can use, and the labor I can still handle at age seventy. I do not want a crop that needs too much hand labor or carries too much market risk. Since I am educated, I pay attention to input efficiency, not just output, so I will use better seed, keep fertilizer balanced instead of chasing yield blindly with nitrogen, and time irrigation around the crop’s critical stages. For wheat, I will focus on strong establishment, spring topdressing, and disease control around jointing to heading. For maize, I will plant quickly after wheat harvest, keep population uniform, push phosphorus and potassium enough to support roots and grain filling, and avoid unnecessary sprays. I will use rotary tillage where it helps me manage residues and seedbed quality without adding the heavier cost and effort of deep ploughing every season.
